course.name: A2 Grammar: Everyday Accuracy with Nguyen Minh Ha

topicDescription: Use going to and will for plans, predictions, offers, and promises.

lessons.title: Going to for Plans and Intentions
lessons.objective: Use be going to for plans made before speaking.
lessons.description: Going to links a present subject with a prior plan or intention.
lessons.content: Use am, is, or are going to plus the base verb for a planned future action.
examples: I am going to visit my aunt on Saturday.
They are going to study tonight.
commonErrors: Do not use will after going to.
Match am, is, or are with the subject.
lessons.guidedPractice: Underline the planned time, then choose the correct be form and base verb.
lessons.summary: Going to describes a plan or intention decided before now.

lessons.title: Going to for Evidence-Based Predictions
lessons.objective: Use going to for a prediction based on visible evidence.
lessons.description: Present evidence can make a future result seem likely.
lessons.content: Use be going to when what you can see or know now points to a future event.
examples: Look at the clouds. It is going to rain.
The child is tired, so she is going to sleep.
commonErrors: Do not use a past form after going to.
Use the subject's correct be form.
lessons.guidedPractice: Identify the evidence first, then choose going to for the likely result.
lessons.summary: Going to can predict a result when present evidence supports it.

lessons.title: Will for Decisions, Offers, and Promises
lessons.objective: Use will for a decision made at speaking time, an offer, or a promise.
lessons.description: Will often responds to a new situation rather than a plan made earlier.
lessons.content: Use will plus the base verb for quick decisions, offers, and promises.
examples: The phone is ringing. I will answer it.
I will help you with that bag.
commonErrors: Do not add to after will.
Do not use will to describe every prior plan.
lessons.guidedPractice: Look for a new situation, an offer, or a promise made now.
lessons.summary: Will expresses a spontaneous decision, offer, or promise.

lessons.title: Choosing Will or Going to
lessons.objective: Choose will or going to from a clear everyday context.
lessons.description: The context tells us whether the idea is a prior plan, evidence-based prediction, or decision now.
lessons.content: Use going to for earlier plans and present evidence; use will for offers, promises, and decisions made now.
examples: We planned it, so we are going to meet.
The phone rings, so I will answer it.
commonErrors: Do not choose only by the time word.
Check whether the plan existed before the conversation.
lessons.guidedPractice: Label each context plan, evidence, or decision now before choosing the form.
lessons.summary: Going to and will have different uses in clear contexts.

questions.questionText: We planned it last week. Choose the best completion: We ___ tomorrow.
questions.explanation: The cue shows the intended use, so are going to meet fits best.
